items.statement: Readiness questionnaires describe self-management knowledge and skills but predict engagement after transfer poorly; continuity with adult clinicians and joint clinics matter more, so readiness assessment should inform planning rather than set the timing of transfer.
items.rationale: Consistent with the measurement review, the prospective study and the qualitative work; directly informs the steering group.
items.risks: Evidence mostly from type 1 diabetes and single sites.

items.statement: Adapted, supported and translated readiness assessments reduce the disadvantage that standard questionnaires create for young people with learning disabilities or low health literacy.
items.rationale: Supported by adaptation studies; evidence thin.
items.risks: No outcome data for adapted tools.

summary: Two working propositions; h1 selected as the organising argument.
